title: Guru Mahima + Maha Sukshma Sharir (quantum level) + 4 Sukshma Tattvas - Base

segments.text: Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 2)
Topic: Guru Mahima, the Maha Sukshma Sharir at the Quantum Level & the Four Sukshma Tattvas

Source: Bhaiya's satsang session (video transcript, ~1hr 20min), part of the ongoing Surya Vigyan series. Previous session covered: the Maha Sukshma Sharir's vice-versa concept, sankalp shakti, and its diﬀer ential combinations. Purpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version.
1. SESSION CONTEXT

This session continues the Surya Vigyan (Science of the Sun) branch of vidyas that Gurudev is unwinding through Bhaiya. Bhaiya shares that Gurudev (Baba) has a strict order that he cannot stay overnight in Aashray, because shaktis arrive there in "dharan" form which clash (pratilopan) with the various sukshma sharirs of a physical body. Earlier, Gurudev used to tell Bhaiya the session content 10–15 minutes in advance. Now Gurudev keeps even Bhaiya in suspense until the very end of the session — Bhaiya learns the teaching at the same moment the listeners do. ("Ko nahi jaanat hai jag mein, Kapi Sankat Mochan naam tiharo" — who in this world does not know your name, O remover of crises.) Recap of the previous session's core lesson: the Maha Sukshma Sharir has its own sankalp (resolve). It itself breaks any sankalp of yours that goes against it. Therefore "You can't blame God for anything you do, because it's your own body" — our own karma makes our sankalps and our own karma breaks them.
2. GURU MAHIMA — CHOOSING A GURU
Think before choosing; never look back after
A person should think not 100 times, not a thousand, not a lakh — but "sahasra koti" (countless crores of) times before deciding who their Guru is. But once the decision is made, never turn back.
Why a human cannot be the ultimate Guru

The human body has a tiny memory. Bhaiya's own words: "I don't even remember what I ate last week — what could I possibly tell you about yourself? How can I be a Guru?" A human's capacity is limited; Guru-hood belongs to the tattva that has knowledge of every tattva. "Jis tattva ko har tattva ka gyaan hai, wahi Guru tattva hai — and that alone is the supreme truth (Satyam Shivam Sundaram)." A Guru is made a worthy vehicle (yogya vaahan) — people wrongly treat guru-hood as a joke, an ego trip of being worshipped, having feet pressed, being called "Guru ji, Guru ji." Critique of the claim "you cannot progress without a human guru": Bhaiya says this claim exists because otherwise "the gurus' shops would shut down." The Guru who resides in every particle (kan-kan) is the one truly worthy of being Guru.
What a true Guru is

A Guru is not one who hands everything over as a gift. A Guru is one who shows the path and says: "I stand with you. If you do it, good; if not, your choice." Gurudev has always worked exactly this way. You may ask Gurudev for any vidya — he never refuses. He will tell you the way; the doing is on you. "If you do it, I give my word — you will become the truth (sat) of it."
Pray directly to Gurudev, not to Bhaiya

In Aashray, whoever comes and accepts Gurudev's shakti receives direct instruction from Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself. Bhaiya explicitly says he does not know the ABC of many tattvas. When people come and directly ask him "what is the solution to this problem?", he too is confused. But when a person ﬁrst prays to Gurudev and then comes, the answer is already with Bhaiya — because Gurudev has already instructed what is to be done. "Call out to the Guru from any corner; if Gurudev orders it, this brother may come to you barefoot." Real example shared: Gurudev once ordered Bhaiya to go somewhere barefoot with turn-byturn directions ("left at the corner house, ﬁrst ﬂoor, she will be sitting at the mandir — sit there, then say this"), revealing instructions step-by-step. The Guru keeps his instrument in suspense; the devotee's prayer is what moves everything.
3. CAN HANUMAN JI MAHARAJ BE YOUR GURU? — YES
People ask: "Hanuman Ji Maharaj is so great and we are so small — can he really be our Guru?" Bhaiya's answer:
Greatness = being the biggest while remaining the smallest

"How does one become truly big? By remaining small even while being big." Paramatma is the greatest precisely because He resides in every particle (kan-kan mein virajit). The one who can dwell in the smallest of the small is the greatest of all.
The Science of Mantra proof

(Taught earlier by Bhaiya at Aqua Foundation as "Science of Mantra.") Hanuman Ji Maharaj's mantra has crossed the 5th dimension of the physical world. When a mantra crosses the physical world's 5th dimension, the being can be present in countless places at the same time, in a fully awakened (jagrit) state. This is why only Hanuman Ji Maharaj and Shanidev carry the boon of remaining awakened on this earth throughout Kalyug. Hanuman Ji is awakened in every particle. Getting the tarang (energy-wave) of Bhagwan Ram, Shiv, Krishna, or the true Mata is very diﬃcult and slow . But Hanuman Ji Maharaj's tarang may be received in as little as three days — that is how awakened this deva is. Who could be a greater Guru? The "Jai Siya Ram" mantra awakens at 1.5 crore (15 million) repetitions — because it is extremely sukshma, and the more sukshma, the more powerful.
If you adopt him as Guru

If you take Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj as your Guru, you will receive according to your grahan shakti (capacity to receive) — whether gyaan (knowledge), shakti (power), or aishwarya (prosperity) — because your Guru is Hanuman Ji Maharaj himself. "Wear Gurudev Shri Hanuman Ji Maharaj on your head as Guru — the prets (negative entities) won't even understand what is going on." "Hanumat ne sabko yeh samjhaya — bina sadhna kisne paya?" (Hanuman taught everyone: nothing is ever attained without sadhna.) Gurudev teaches; the sadhak must still do the sadhna. As sadhnas are completing, miracles in Aashray are increasing day by day — some sadhnas have already fructiﬁed (people r eceiving their Kul Devta's kripa, vidyas awakening), others are in progress.
4. MAHA SUKSHMA SHARIR — THE QUANTUM-LEVEL CORRECTION
The big misunderstanding

People hear "MAHA sukshma sharir" and imagine something huge and towering. Wrong. Sukshma = small. Maha-sukshma = the ultimately small — smaller than the smallest, subtler than the subtle (ati-sukshma). Think quantum/nano level. This is why
quantum physics and quantum chemistry are in vogue — they work on the smallest particles. Mantra has always been sukshma.
The core law: the smaller, the more powerful

"Jitna sukshma, utna prabhavshali" — the subtler something is, the more powerful it is, and the closer it is to Paramatma. Our human scaling system is ﬂawed: we always look upward (bigger must be greater). In the astral world the scale runs downward — smaller is greater. Paramatma resides in every particle precisely because He is the most sukshma. The Maha Sukshma Sharir is an ansh (fragment) of Paramatma within us. Because it is so small: it cannot be seen (big things are visible to all; the small thing is not), and it cannot be broken or killed — nothing possesses the capacity to harm it. "The one who works on the sukshma tattva is the one who creates at the level of principle (siddhantik nirmaan)" — the next principle of Surya Vigyan.
The straw (tinka) & God-particle analogy

Put weight on a whole arm — it breaks. Cut it in half — capacity increases. Keep making it smaller — capacity keeps increasing. A single straw withstands the full atmospheric pressure upon it. The smallest thing bears the greatest load. Science reference: the God particle (Higgs boson) experiment was devised to measure how much pressure/energy a single tiny particle can withstand when a proton is accelerated to maximum speed — "where did so much shakti come from in that one particle?" Therefore the Maha Sukshma Sharir holds atulit shakti (immeasurable power) — and Bajrangbali Maharaj possesses atulit shakti because he is the subtlest of the subtle.
Energy exchange with your Maha Sukshma Sharir

The shakti of all four sukshma sharirs (see Section 5) is ONE — it is never separate. It can be diverted, channelized, and converted from one form to another ("Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be converted from one form to another"). The real shakti of your body resides in the Maha Sukshma Sharir. It works like an electrolyte: the more positive signs you create, the more keeps ﬂowing to you. Asymmetry: the Maha Sukshma Sharir can draw energy from you eﬀortlessly . But for YOU to draw energy from it, you must make yourself sukshma — go smaller/subtler (humbler) than it. You cannot pull energy "upward" from below; that is against universal law, not enmity. This is exactly why so much jaap is needed. Practical instruction: become small. "Kuchh nahi karna — chhota hona hai. Thoda milega." (Nothing else to do — become small, and you will receive.) Adopting Hanuman Ji as Guru and becoming "his alone" is the fastest way to understand this.
5. THE FOUR SUKSHMA TATTVAS (Categories of the Sukshma Sharir)
Gurudev revealed in this session that the sukshma sharir has four categories of tattvas: Gan Tattva, Atma Tattva, Nirman Tattva, and Ghor Tattva.
5.1 Gan Tattva

Every person has it (always active). It deﬁnes a person's "gan" — the quality elders referred to when saying "iska gan tez hai" (his/her gan is strong). Gan = linked to sankalp shakti (strength of resolve). A person with a strong gan: the evil eye (nazar) does not aﬀect them , they do not fall ill easily, and their works get done quickly. If two people receive nazar, the one with the strong gan is unaﬀected — this sukshma sharir repels it. The gan tattva diﬀers fr om person to person.
5.2 Atma Tattva

Every person has it (always active). A sukshma sharir that stays joined to your atma tattva — carrying the position and/or the mantra that was running with you from past lives. This is connected to prarabdha: roughly 70–78% of the sadhna-bal (accumulated spiritual merit) earned in previous births is visible in this atma tattva. This is what people mean when they say "yeh peechhe se bahut achha lekar aaya hai" (this one has brought great merit from before).
5.3 Nirman Tattva

NOT active in everyone. Unlike the ﬁrst two, this tattva must be asked for, or activated. When activated, paralaukik (otherworldly) shaktis begin to form in the person — this sukshma sharir connects you to the paralaukik jagat. Sudden creativity (a person becoming remarkably "creative" after a certain age, beyond ordinary drawing/painting innovation) is described as a sign of this connection. All the sadhnas running in Aashray — talking to Baba, receiving vidyas, all darshanrelated work — operate on the Nirman Tattva. Gurudev communicates with Bhaiya through this very sukshma sharir. Keep working on it continuously ("Prabhu, come and teach us") and Gurudev will keep guiding further.
5.4 Ghor Tattva

The ﬁercest and most diﬃcult tattva ("ghor = that which is very, very diﬃcult"; distinct from "aghor," covered earlier). Position (as revealed): it hangs like a ball tied by two cords, about eight ﬁnger-widths below the reproductive organ, between the two legs, and appears completely black in color. Connection to Maa Chhinnamasta: one of the 10 Mahavidyas (famous temple at Rajrappa, Jharkhand). Look at her iconography — she stands upon a copulating couple (kaam), and the garland hanging between the legs marks exactly the ghor-tattva point. Secret (gupt) sadhnas of Maa Chhinnamasta — still practiced quietly in Bengal and several regions — work directly on the ghor tattva. Chhinnamasta katha: the demon Raktabeej had a boon — wherever a drop of his blood fell, a new Raktabeej would instantly arise. Mata took this form to destroy him: she drank every drop of his blood before it could touch the earth. She severed her own head and drank her own blood to quench the thirst/hunger of her attendants Dakini and Shakini. Powers: one who awakens the ghor tattva (or makes it work) is said to gain the shaktis of the seven lower lokas — authority over 1400 lokas. Dangers: it is extremely dangerous. It requires a Guru who awakens only that tattva. When a person adopts this sukshma sharir, no one can bear to live near them — it is the anti/opposite of the ordinary sukshma sharir. Some compare it to a black hole (though, as Bhaiya notes, the original tattvas were made inside the body ﬁrst — that is why they also appear in the universal galaxy). Merely speaking its name attracts entities from the lower lokas. During the session itself, Bhaiya paused ("give me 2 minutes") to clear the energies that had gathered, explaining that everything spoken there is spoken before Bhagwan Ram, by whose order every shakti stays in check — otherwise everyone's "battery" (energy) in the session would have drained.
Rules across the four tattvas

Working on one main sukshma sharir reduces the ugrata (intensity) of the others. No one has ever lived with all four sukshma sharirs awakened. Even the devas and Mata took diﬀer ent forms/avatars to awaken these sukshma sharirs separately. Many permutations and combinations of these tattvas exist — but everything depends on the Guru. The Guru is the key: he summons the appropriate siddhis of your principal form from past lives, as he deems ﬁt. "If the Guru is right, everything is completely right."
Warning on sadhna "crazes"
Nowadays there is a craze for Dhumavati Mata sadhna; before that the craze was Pishachini, Yakshini, Dakini, Shakini; Baglamukhi is "evergreen" (especially among

politicians); Kamakhya Devi likewise draws crowds. Implicit warning (consistent with Session 1): do not chase ﬁer ce/ugra sadhnas out of fashion — the ghor tattva realm is dangerous and requires exactly the right specialized Guru.

Core laws to remember: 1. The smaller (more sukshma) something is, the more powerful it is and the closer to Paramatma. 2. The Maha Sukshma Sharir = the ultimately small fragment of Paramatma in you; unbreakable, invisible, holding your real shakti. 3. To receive energy from the subtle, become subtle (humble) yourself — this is universal law, and why continuous jaap matters. 4. The four tattvas share ONE shakti; it can only be converted/channelized, never created or destroyed. 5. Work on one main sukshma sharir; never attempt all four. 6. Choose your Guru after countless deliberation — then never look back. The safest, greatest Guru: Hanuman Ji Maharaj, awakened in every particle in Kalyug. 7. Nothing is attained without sadhna — the Guru shows the path; the walking is yours. 8. Pray to Gurudev directly before seeking solutions; the answer reaches you through his instrument.
